problems: The paper map renders almost pure white, so it doesn't read as a cream paper map. Its color is too pale and the light washes it out; it needs a deeper, warmer cream.

The three tilted, overlapping map panels don't read as folds. They make one stray thin line through the handle and an odd wedge of table in the lower-left corner. A single flat sheet that clearly lies on the dark table reads better.
The dark wooden table renders as a light tan patch in only one corner. It should be a darker wood brown, and the map should be placed so the table shows as a clean strip along the card edges.
The gold neck between the rim and the ferrule floats about 0.01 above the paper. Lower it so it lines up with the rim tube and the ferrule, which rest on the paper.
The construction and framing are sound. The rim and handle rest flat on the paper, the neck and ferrule join them, and the glass fills most of the card on its main body.
The cream map renders almost pure white under the high light, so it does not read as cream paper. Darken and warm the paper color.
The handle reads as a medium, pinkish brown rather than the brief's dark brown. Darken it and give it a matte wood finish instead of satin, so the highlight does not wash it out.
